title: Buffalo Sabres sign Noah Östlund to eight-year, $52.8 million extension
content:
BUFFALO, N.Y. — The Buffalo Sabres have signed forward Noah Östlund to an eight-year contract extension worth $6.6 million per year, the team announced Monday.

Östlund, a first-round draft pick in 2022, got his first regular NHL action last season. He played in 60 games and had 11 goals and 16 assists. He also had a goal and an assist in three playoff games against the Bruins before sustaining a lower-body injury.

Östlund had one year remaining on his entry-level contract, but the Sabres moved early to lock up a rising young forward while eight-year contracts are still allowed under the collective bargaining agreement. (The new CBA comes into effect Tuesday, which restricts the maximum length to seven years.) The only knock on Östlund early in his pro career has been injuries, but his playmaking skills, defensive awareness and tenacity have all helped him transition quickly to the NHL.

Going back to his draft year, Sabres assistant general manager Jerry Forton was wowed by Östlund’s competitiveness and hockey smarts.

“He’s always been very good at scoring in tight and around the net, a little bit like a poor man’s Jake Guentzel in that regard,” Forton said. “His hockey sense, his edges, his compete and tight areas skills would have reminded us of a Jake Guentzel type, but a different player projecting him at the NHL level. We view Noah as a pure center and more of a distributor and pass-first guy.”

Strength was the one big question on Östlund coming into the draft, and that hasn’t been entirely answered yet. He won only 31 percent of his face-offs during the regular season last year and needs to get stronger in that department if he’s going to stick as a center long-term. But the Sabres are betting on continued growth from Östlund, and that $6.6 million cap hit could look extremely team-friendly in a few years if he continues to develop the way he has.
